text.p: Merrill Lynch in London has raised its rating for Poland's Bank Slaski to accumulate from neutral and its long-term view to buy after the share's recent fall on the Warsaw bourse, Merrill said in a report.
"With Slaski's shares down 31-percent in dollar terms this year, we are raising our intermediate-term opinion from neutral to accumulate and our long-term view to buy," the report dated July 18 said.
Slaski is 54.1-percent controlled by ING Bank.

Merrill lowered its 1997 and 1998 net income forecasts by six and 15 percent to 243 million and 277 million zlotys due to more expected price wars for lending and deposits in the consumer segment and concerns about a central bank rate rise.
But it called its 1998 price-earnings ratio for the bank of 7.1 and price-net-asset-value ratio of 1.3 attractive for investors with a time horizon extending to mid-1998.
"By then, we believe, the market should recognise the benefits of investments in information technology, an expanded distribution network and organisational restructuring currently underway."
Merrill said such investment should support 10-percent real earnings growth from 1999 to 2003 and five percent thereafter.

It said it was less confident of Slaski's shares' performance in 1997 as the market seemed focused on negative trends in interest margins and provisions which were likely to produce poor operating results through 1998.
